comments: The Department of Defense (DoD) expanded the footprint of small business participation in the Defense Industrial Base in FY 2024 with an increase of $4.9B in contract awards to small businesses. The DoD’s overall performance garnered an "A" rating overall for the SBA’s FY24 agency small business scorecard. Of note, there was an increase of $2.5B awarded to small disadvantaged businesses (SDBs), an increase of over $100M in contracts to women owned small businesses (WOSB), an increase of over $800M to service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSB), and over $200M to HUBZone companies. An additional $56.8B was subcontracted to small businesses from DoD's large prime suppliers. The 90+ APEX Accelerators across the country and DoD Mentor-Protégé Program continues to provide a robust footprint and platform to cultivate companies to acquire the capabilities to become suppliers of critical technologies and services necessary for supply chain resilience and bolstering deterrence.

comments:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury is pleased to earn an improved score of an A+ on the FY24 scorecard. Treasury’s FY 2024 small business goal was set at 37% and Treasury exceeded the goal by 2.9%, achieving 39.95%. Treasury obligated $3.7 billion in prime contract dollars to small businesses, an increase of $100M over FY 2023 small business obligations. 
Treasury’s commitment to providing opportunities for small disadvantaged businesses resulted in FY24 obligations of $1.4 billion to SDBs, an increase of $200 million over FY 2023 SDB obligations, for a remarkable 1.2% increase. In FY24, Treasury exceeded its Women Owned Small Business goal of 5%, awarding 9.8% of its total obligations, or $899.4 million; exceeded its Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business goal of 5%, with SVDVSB participation reaching 8.04%, or $738.4 million; and nearly doubled its 3% goal for HUBZone Business awards, awarding 5.95% or $546.1 million to HUBZone businesses. 
As we celebrate the remarkable accomplishment of achieving an A+ on SBA scorecard for FY 2024, it is essential to acknowledge that this success could not have been realized without the unwavering support of the Treasury acquisition workforce and leaders throughout the Department.  By establishing clear priorities and encouraging a whole-of-Treasury approach, we continue to create an ecosystem that drives economic prosperity but also enhances taxpayer compliance.	This transformative effort aims to position the nation as a leader in innovation, ensuring that the benefits of technological advancements are accessible to all Americans.	 
In FY 2025, we will focus on expanding our efforts underscoring on transparency, cost savings, and efficiencies, fostering further collaboration among our internal and external stakeholders.  The integration of digital platforms and technological advancements, particularly through the infusion of AI and bots, is revolutionizing the way the Treasury OSDBU market research will be conducted and shared, creating a dynamic repository of insights that empowers small businesses and the 1101/1102 acquisition community to make informed decisions.	By fostering a robust business partnership network, Treasury prime contractors and small businesses can leverage these advance tools to enhance collaboration, drive innovation, and unlock new opportunities in an increasingly competitive landscape.
In essence, this achievement of an A+ on Treasury SBA Scorecard serves as a pivotal Call to Action, urging our internal and external stakeholders at all levels to collaborate in building a robust adaptable, and future-ready economy that meets the challenges of the 21st century.

comments: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is honored to receive an annual procurement scorecard rating of "A", from the Small Business Administration (SBA).  The recognition represents significant accomplishments made by HUD to create contracting opportunities for small business concerns in all categories.	 For FY 2024, HUD exceeded its annual small business and women-owned small business prime goals.  This achievement was due to the collaborative efforts of the program offices, procurement, OSDBU staff, and the Department's senior leadership.  HUD conducted nationwide outreach events and trainings covering topics such as: access to capital, understanding the U.S. General Services Administration’s (GSA) contract vehicles and category management, and marketing to government agencies.  HUD also continued convening its signature annual Information Technology Industry Day and outreach events for Women-Owned, HUBZone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned small businesses.	 These critical advocacy efforts inform small businesses of the opportunities at HUD and across the federal marketplace.  HUD also remains committed to educating its acquisition workforce and clients on changes in acquisition policies and regulations that impact small business utilization and programs.	 With its robust acquisition planning processes, the Department is committed to empowering America’s entrepreneurs and job creators and will continue to identify areas to maximize practicable opportunities for small businesses in both prime and subcontracting opportunities.

comments:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) remains fully committed to supporting its mission and operations through Federal acquisitions with small businesses to drive innovation, optimize efficiency and cost savings, support domestic manufacturing, and boost U.S. investment. All of which contributes to the agency achieving its statutorily mandated small business economic goals and entrepreneurial targets.

The agency's Small Business Program has implemented a compliance, technical assistance, and training program designed to maximize prime and subcontract opportunities for small businesses and entrepreneurs. The interdependency and collaboration between the Small Business Program, purchasing offices, and the agency’s acquisition team throughout the acquisition planning and market research stages of procurement was vital towards driving success. As a testament to our commitment, the agency exceeded four out of five of its small business prime contract economic goals, nearly achieved its increased service-disabled veteran-owned small business goal, which we missed by less than half of a percent. However, a strategic remedial action plan has been developed to improve economic opportunities for the Nation’s veterans, and this plan’s activities have been incorporated into our procurement process.

The agency is dedicated to driving transformative growth for small businesses by amplifying opportunities through strategic efforts and the Small Business Program’s legislatively mandated responsibilities. Moving forward, the Small Business Program will continue to implement targeted activities to identify efficiencies and cost saving measures, refine agency resources, enhance our virtual event series, harness cutting-edge technology to enhance marketplace analysis, and employ innovative procurement practices to strengthen competition and the domestic supplier base.
